title: Ops Pocket Guide: Controls, Change, Data, Procurement & Templates
author: Asha Patel
body:
Summary
-------
This pocket guide consolidates Redwood-wide controls and step-by-step processes for access and permissions, change management, data governance, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel exceptions, and packaged internal templates. It is intended as a single-stop reference for team leads, people-ops partners, engineering managers, finance approvers, and security reviewers.

Scope
-----
Applies to all company employees, contractors, and third-party vendors that interact with Redwood systems and data. Exceptions must be documented and approved by the owning team and Security.

1) Access and Permissions Lifecycle
----------------------------------
Goal: Ensure least-privilege, auditable access provisioning and timely deprovisioning.

Key services and tools
- Redwood IAM (central identity store; SSO + SCIM provisioning)
- Jira Service Desk (access request and approvals)
- Okta for SSO and MFA enforcement
- Vault (secrets management)

Roles and responsibilities
- Requester: Submits access request and justification.
- Manager: Verifies business need and signs approval (within 72 hours).
- Resource Owner: Grants or denies access, documents duration and justification.
- Security: Performs periodic audit and exception reviews.

Standard request flow (numbered)
1. Requester files access request in Jira Service Desk using template "Access Request - Role/Resource".
2. Manager approves in Jira within 72 hours. Auto-escalate to skip-level after 96 hours.
3. Resource Owner assigns role and logs entitlement in the Access Log.
4. SCIM provisioning applies role in Redwood IAM; Okta pushes group membership to services.
5. After 90 days, access expires unless renewed via a Renewal Request.

Temporary access and emergency access
- Temporary access (duration <= 14 days) requires manager approval and must specify start/end dates.
- Emergency access (breakglass) is permitted only when a production incident requires immediate work. Broken-glass sessions must be opened in the Breakglass Tracker and reviewed within 48 hours by Security.

Periodic audits and attestations
- Quarterly entitlement review by Resource Owners.
- Access attestation cadence: Engineering and Product: quarterly; Finance and Legal: biannually.
- SLO: 95% of stale access remediated within 30 days of detection.

2) Change Management (Service & Configuration Changes)
-----------------------------------------------------
Purpose: Coordinate changes to services and infra to reduce risk and ensure rollback capability.

Change types and approval matrix
- Standard changes: Low-risk, pre-approved templates (e.g., routine config refresh). No CAB required; change owner posts in #changes Slack channel 24h prior.
- Normal changes: Non-emergency changes that may impact availability or behaviour. Require change ticket in Jira, risk assessment, and CAB sign-off if risk level >= medium.
- Emergency changes: High-priority fixes for active incidents. Notify SRE and Security, document post-facto, and schedule a post-incident review.

CAB (Change Advisory Board) composition and cadence
- Weekly CAB meeting: SRE lead, Release Manager, Product Ops, Security representative, and an affected service owner.
- Ad-hoc CAB for high-severity normal changes.

Change process (high level)
1. Create Jira change ticket with: description, risk rating, rollback plan, monitoring playbook, and expected impact window.
2. Run canary deploys in staging and execute smoke-tests.
3. Submit to CAB at least 48 hours before planned change (unless emergency).
4. Post-deploy: update runbook, close ticket only after 24h stability window.

Required artifacts for every normal change
- Runbook link
- Rollback steps (exact CLI/commands or job id)
- Impact matrix (services impacted and owners)
- Observability checklist: dashboards to monitor and alerts to mute

3) Data Management & Classification
----------------------------------
Objective: Protect data according to sensitivity and legal requirements while enabling productive access.

Classification levels (table-style text)
- PUBLIC: Information safe for public disclosure (docs, marketing website).
- INTERNAL: Company information intended for internal use only; minimal risk if leaked.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Contains PII, contract terms, customer-provided data with restrictions. Requires encryption at rest and in transit, and RBAC-enforced access.
- RESTRICTED: Highest sensitivity (regulated data, keys, or production secrets). Access only to explicitly approved individuals and logged via Vault.

Retention and deletion guidelines
- Default retention: product telemetry 365 days; aggregated metrics: indefinitely.
- PII: retain only as necessary for business purpose; default retention 2 years unless customer contract requires longer.
- Data deletion: Data owners must create a Deletion Request in Jira with a data inventory and deletion proof (screenshot or deleted object IDs).

Encryption and key management
- All CONFIDENTIAL and RESTRICTED data at rest must be encrypted with keys managed in KMS/HSM.
- Access to key material is permissioned via Vault policies.

Data access request flow
1. Submit Data Access Request (Jira) including dataset name, columns, justification, and duration.
2. Data Steward reviews within 5 business days.
3. If approved, access provisioned in query environment (read-only) or via extract with minimized fields.

4) Procurement & Expenses (Buttons to buy the right things)
----------------------------------------------------------
Principles: Centralize vendor spend, enforce approvals by spend tier, and preserve audit trail for reimbursements.

Procurement thresholds and approvers (table-style text)
- <$1,000: Manager approval (use expense reimbursement).
- $1,000-$25,000: Manager + Finance approver.
- $25,000-$250,000: Manager + Finance + Legal review.
- >$250,000: VP approval + Legal + Procurement committee.

Preferred vendor platforms
- SaaS procurement: Coupa (ProcureFlow) for contract and purchase order lifecycle.
- Hardware/Capital: Request via "HW Request" template in Jira and route to IT Asset Management.

Procurement process (numbered)
1. Fill the procurement request template in Coupa or Jira (item, justification, cost center, expected contract term).
2. Finance verifies budget and assigns GL codes within 3 business days.
3. Legal performs contract review for spend >= $25k or if data handling clauses exist.
4. Procurement issues PO and routes to vendor.
5. Receipts and invoices: upload to Expense system and tag to PO.

Expense reimbursement rules
- Use corporate card for approved recurring SaaS or travel.
- Expense submission window: within 30 days of spend. Late submissions require People Ops review and may be denied.
- Per diem: follows regional brackets on the Travel Matrix (see Travel policy section).

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding Checklist
-----------------------------------------
Objective: Ensure vendors meet security, privacy, and contractual standards before granting access or engaging financially.

Vendor onramp checklist (each item required for medium/high risk vendors):
- Business case and owner assigned.
- Security questionnaire completed (SSQ) and reviewed by InfoSec.
- Contract with data processing addendum (DPA) and SLAs if applicable.
- Classification of vendor data access (scope & least privilege).
- Insurance and compliance evidence (ISO/ SOC reports) if handling CONFIDENTIAL or RESTRICTED data.
- Vendor access provisioning tickets and least-privilege roles created in Redwood IAM.
- Quarterly vendor risk review scheduled for ongoing vendors.

Vendor offboarding steps
1. Raise Offboard ticket in Jira with last date of work.
2. Revoke all credentials and rotate shared secrets.
3. Confirm data return/deletion per contract and document with proof.
4. Close vendor account and archive contract in procurement system.

6) Travel Policy & Exceptions
-----------------------------
Standard travel policy highlights
- All business travel requires pre-approval via Travel Request form and alignment with cost center.
- Travelers must use approved booking vendors for airfare and hotels.
- Travel insurance for international trips above 7 days is required.

Expense caps (examples)
- Domestic lodging cap: $250/night (regional exceptions require pre-approval).
- International lodging cap: $350/night.
- Meals: per diem follows published regional table in Travel Matrix.

Exceptions and approval workflow
- Exceptions to policy (e.g., upgraded seat class, additional nights) must be requested 7+ days in advance and require manager + Finance approval.
- Emergency extension: manager approval and post-trip expense justification required.

7) Internal Templates & Artifacts Index
--------------------------------------
The following templates are pre-approved and available in the Templates Library (Confluence):
- Access Request - Role/Resource (Jira template id: AR-2025)
- Change Ticket Template (CT-std) with rollback checklist
- Data Access Request (DAR-1)
- Vendor Onboarding Checklist (VENDOR-ON-2024)
- Procurement Request Form (PROC-REQ)
- Travel Request & Expense Form (TRV-REQ)
- Incident Breakglass Report (BGR-1)

8) Escalation Paths & Contacts
------------------------------
- Security incidents: PagerDuty -> Security on-call; also open Security Incident ticket.
- Procurement exceptions: Finance Manager -> Head of Finance.
- Access disputes: People Ops -> Security -> Legal if contractual.

9) Compliance, Reporting, and KPIs
----------------------------------
Suggested metrics to track (examples)
- Average time to provision new access: target <= 48 hours.
- Percentage of change tickets with complete rollback plans: target 100%.
- Vendor onboarding SLA (from request to contract signing): target <= 20 business days.
- Data access request median turnaround: <= 5 business days.

Reporting cadence
- Monthly operations dashboard for execs: spend by cost center, outstanding procurement requests, vendor risk summary.
- Quarterly compliance report: access attestation results, audit findings, and remediation status.

10) Exceptions and Continuous Improvement
---------------------------------------
- Exceptions must be documented in Jira with a Business Justification and expiry date, reviewed by Security and People Ops.
- We will run an annual controls retrospective to refine thresholds, templates, and automation points.

Related pages
-------------

Appendices
---------
Appendix A: Quick CLI snippets (examples)
- Revoke group membership in Redwood IAM (example):
  curl -X POST https://iam.redwood.internal/api/v1/revoke -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"user":"alice@example.com","group":"infra-admins"}'

Appendix B: Contact directory (roles only)
- Security: security-oncall@redwood.com
- Finance: procure-team@redwood.com
- People Ops: people-ops@redwood.com
